We'll teach you, we will, we'll pound it into your head, that things you once did without thinking, like eating, drinking, things you did freely, spontaneously, with the ease of unknowing, you've been doing all wrong, and that now they must be done in regimental order: One and two and three, and so on into infinity. Fact is, this thought machine of ours is like a masterpiece on a weaver’s loom. One pedal stirs a thousand threads, shuttles shooting back and forth, threads flowing unseen, and then a single stroke, and a thousand knots are tied. Yes, yes, and then in comes the philosopher, sure as rain, explaining, explaining: it had to be so, how else could it be? First comes one, and then comes two, and then the three and four come due; and if the one and two hadn’t come, three and four would come undone! What a round of applause that gets from the students— and yet, not one of them ever became a weaver. When scholars want to describe a living thing, they must kill it first. Only then do they have the parts in the palm of their hand, but they’ve lost the whole— the spirit that binds it! Chemists call it manipulating nature, and come out looking fools, but don’t know why.
translation:
@@U00532@@
我们会教你，我们会，我们会把它灌输到你的脑海里，让你知道，你曾经不假思索地做的事情，比如吃、喝，你自由地、自发地、轻松地不知不觉地做的事情，你一直在做错事，而现在它们必须按团的顺序完成：一、二、三，依此类推，直到无穷大。事实上，我们的这个思维机器就像织布机上的杰作。一踏板搅动千丝，梭子来回，丝流无形，一划，结千结。是的，是的，然后哲学家进来了，确定如雨，解释，解释：它必须如此，否则怎么可能呢？首先是一，然后是二，然后是三和四；如果一和二不来，三和四就会失败！学生们响起了热烈的掌声——然而，他们中没有一个人成为了织布工。当学者想要描述一个生物时，他们必须先杀死它。只有这样，他们才掌握了部分，但却失去了整体——束缚它的精神！化学家称之为操纵自然，结果看起来很傻，但不知道为什么。
